sources.citation: Chacko, Sajayan & Liahey Ngwazah (Juliana Kelsall, series ed.). 2012. Sociolinguistic survey of selected Rajasthani speech varieties of Rajasthan, India, Volume 6: Marwari, Merwari, and Godwari. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2012-034. 58 pp. (Internet Archive copy of sil.org reapdata PDF)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (RTT, Hindi SRT, questionnaires) plus 210-item wordlists from Merwari sites (Degana/Nagaur, Badlya/Ajmer) with no stress marks. Sec. 1.3: 'Merwari circuit' = Ajmer + Nagaur, also called Ajmeri, speakers consider themselves Marwari speakers; sec. 1.4 names Gusain 2004 (Marwari, LINCOM) as the only grammatical description.

sources.citation: Samuvel, Nelson, Marshall Joshua, Binoy Koshy & Binny Abraham. 2012. Sociolinguistic survey of selected Rajasthani speech varieties of Rajasthan, India, Volume 1: Preliminary overview. SIL ESR 2012-029.
sources.note: Nothing (zero hits for stress/accent/tone); Merwari wordlists from Munduva (Nagaur), Ajmer, Dourai, Jhuniya (Ajmer).

sources.citation: Mukherjee, Kakali. 2011. Marwari. In: Linguistic Survey of India: LSI-Rajasthan Part I, 29-142. Kolkata: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India.
sources.note: 2.1.2 'Suprasegmental Phoneme: Suprasegmentation is significantly realised in Nasalisation' -- no stress statement; describes (Jodhpur-type) Marwari, not Merwari.

sources.citation: Rastogi, Kavita (ed.). 2003. Bhashavigyan paribhasha kosh [Dictionary of linguistic terminology]. (Hindi.) archive.org dli.language.1114
sources.note: Entry 'samatan sima rekha' (isotone) remarks in passing that in Merwari (Hindi area) the word 'kil' spoken with a particular pitch (sur) means 'orhni' (veil) -- an unsourced third-hand hint at a pitch contrast; nothing on stress placement.

sources.citation: Bahri, Hardev. [1965, reprints]. Hindi: udbhav, vikas aur rup. Allahabad: Kitab Mahal. sec. 4.6.1 Marwari (names Ajmer-Merwara as a mixed-Marwari area).
sources.note: Nothing on stress; notes implosive-like sounds and morphology of Marwari only.

sources.citation: Voegelin, C. F. & F. M. Voegelin. 1965. Languages of the world: Indo-European fascicle one. Anthropological Linguistics 7(8) (ERIC ED010363); Rajasthani pp. 255-257 ('Marwari (Merwari, Mewari)').
sources.note: Dialect geography after Grierson only; no stress statement for Rajasthani.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.) 1908. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX: Indo-Aryan family, Central group, Part II: Specimens of the Rajasthani and Gujarati. Calcutta. pp. 70 (Ajmer-Merwara), 76 (Marwari of Merwara), 84 (Mewari: Merwari).
sources.note: Nothing. p. 84: Merwari 'in no way differs from ordinary Mewari, and specimens are unnecessary'; p. 70: Merwari 'practically the same as the Mewari of the State of Mewar'; no pronunciation/accent paragraph for Merwari, Mewari or Eastern Marwari (accent appears only in the front-matter transliteration key).

sources.citation: Kellogg, S. H. 1893. A grammar of the Hindi language.. also the colloquial dialects of Rajputana.. 2nd ed. London: Kegan Paul. (treats 'Mairwari', the dialect of Mairwara in the northern Aravallis, secs. 3a, 111-112, 129 and verb paradigms)
sources.note: Only general/High-Hindi accent remarks (sec. 35 accent weak and subordinate to quantity; sec. 415 accent in causals); nothing on accent in Mairwari. Silent for this language.

sources.citation: Devy, G. N. (chief ed.), Madan Meena & Suraj Rao (eds). 2017. The Languages of Rajasthan. People's Linguistic Survey of India, vol. 25 part 2. Hyderabad: Orient BlackSwan. 320 pp. ISBN 9788125063971 (ebook 9789352871339). Chapter 16: Merwari.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only located work with a chapter on Merwari itself (publisher TOC verified); PLSI chapters usually give a short phonology/grammar note that may mention stress.

sources.note: Nearest-kin modern description with a phonology chapter incl. suprasegmentals (Gusain's Bagri 1999 sec. 4.3.2 has an explicit stress rule: nouns initial, verbs final); Merwari speakers self-identify as Marwari and Grierson classes Merwari as Eastern Marwari -- would supply the statement second-hand for merw1238 (identity marw1260).
